stories.summary: Korean researchers strengthened biodegradable plastic using hemp hurd — the woody core left over after fibre extraction, normally burned or dumped. Lead with the constraint this addresses: biodegradable plastics have failed commercially on mechanical strength, not on chemistry, so a cheap reinforcing filler is the bottleneck being removed. The reason it matters beyond the lab is the team's claim that the method transfers to soybean stalks and rice straw, which are produced in enormous volume across South and Southeast Asia and are currently burned in the field — a major seasonal air-pollution source from Punjab to the Mekong. The mechanism to explain for the reader: how cellulose fibres carry load inside a polymer matrix, and what 'biodegradable' actually requires in terms of disposal conditions.

stories.label: Mathematicians Build Long-Awaited Graph Sandwich
stories.summary: A decades-old conjecture in graph theory has been proved, giving researchers a new way to decompose complex networks. Lead with what the result lets you do rather than with the abstraction: the 'sandwich' is a way of trapping an arbitrary graph between two well-understood structures, so properties provable for the simple bounds transfer to the messy object in between. For our reader the payoff is where graphs are the model — routing, supply chains, epidemic spread, and the sparse-attention structures underlying large models. Be honest about the gap between a proof and an algorithm: this is an existence result, and the writer should say plainly whether it is constructive.

stories.label: US extends visa ban on Palestinian officials before UN General Assembly
stories.summary: Mahmoud Abbas is barred from the UN General Assembly for the second consecutive year while Washington holds direct talks with Hamas and places no comparable restriction on Israeli officials. Lead with the mechanism, because it is the part wire copy skips: the 1947 UN Headquarters Agreement obliges the United States to grant transit to delegations regardless of bilateral relations, and Washington's standing reservation is a 'national security' carve-out it has invoked before — in 1988 the General Assembly relocated to Geneva rather than accept a denial. Report whether any member state has proposed that remedy this time, what the State Department gave as its ground, and what the PLO delegation says. Who holds power: the host state, whose visa officer can silence a member observer. Who is affected: Palestinians whose only remaining forum is one they can now be locked out of. Contrast explicitly with our 09-18 piece on the US granting visas to Iran's delegation — same agreement, opposite outcome, same week. SELECTION NOTE: the feed carried only 7 multi-source clusters, 2 unusable (Modi's 76th-birthday greetings, entertainment; the Russia/China veto of the Iran sanctions panel, which the 09-17 Pakistan-abstention piece already covered). Politics multi-source floor met with this and the Russian elections piece; economy multi-source floor met with the Saudi pipeline and Buffett — the only two economy clusters in the feed, so neither is a padding pick. Rejected multi-source: the Carpathian Eight summit (ANSA), because it is the same Zelenskyy summit weekend as the Russian-elections entry and Europe is already the heaviest region in the window. OIC SOURCING GAPS for feed-side audit: (1) the Kohat mosque bombing in Pakistan is carried only by NDTV (IN) — no Dawn, Geo or Express Tribune copy of that event appears in the feed, though Dawn is present with three unrelated items; (2) the Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown carries only Bloomberg (US) and Investing.com (IN), no Arab News or Al Jazeera; (3) the Indonesian deficit-ceiling debate carries only The Diplomat (US), no Jakarta Post. Skipped under the sourcing-discipline rule for the third consecutive cycle: Declassified UK's 'Starmer complicit in Trump's Yemen massacre' and three Responsible Statecraft items, all advocacy outlets with no corroborating feed source; also both TASS items on AUKUS, which are uncorroborated Russian foreign-ministry claims from a single state wire.

stories.label: Ukraine fires drone barrage as Russia launches elections
stories.summary: Russia opened polls for its first parliamentary elections since the invasion began while more than 350 Ukrainian drones struck Moscow and other regions on the same morning. Lead with the collision of the two facts — a state holding a vote about a war it is simultaneously being hit by. Teach the mechanism our reader will not get elsewhere: the Duma is elected half by party list and half by single-member districts, candidate registration is controlled administratively before any vote is cast, and remote electronic voting now carries a large share of the ballot in Moscow — so the contested question is not the count but who was permitted onto the ballot. Report the registration exclusions, the turnout claims and who is making them, and what independent monitors are permitted to observe, attributing each. Then the Ukrainian half: report what Moscow's mayor said was intercepted, what was actually struck — refineries appear in the reporting — and Kyiv's stated aim, which is the same supply-chain-targeting doctrine we described in the Polish-warning piece. Who holds power: an administration that sets both the ballot and the war's terms. Who is affected: Russian voters with no unapproved option, and Ukrainians under the reciprocal barrage. Note that the vote extends to occupied territories, which is the part that carries legal consequence.

stories.label: 15 Killed, Over 50 Injured After Suicide Bombing At Mosque In Pakistan
stories.summary: A suicide bomber drove an explosives-laden vehicle into a mosque in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, during Friday prayer: at least 15 dead, 56 injured, five of the dead police officers. Lead with the timing and the place — jumu'ah, a mosque, worshippers — and name the dead as they are identified, because that is the dignity the wire copy will not extend. The mechanism to teach: the mosque adjoined a building housing police offices, which is the pattern in KP — attackers strike the security target through the civilian congregation next to it, so the casualty count is structurally civilian by design. Report who has claimed it or denied it, and be precise about attribution rather than assigning blame by assumption; the TTP and Islamic State-Khorasan both operate in the district and both have disowned mosque attacks before. Then the context our reader needs: KP has absorbed the largest share of Pakistan's post-2021 attack resurgence, the province's police are the most-killed force in the country, and the government's response has moved between negotiation and operations without settling on either. Report the provincial and federal response and what security was in place. Who is affected: a congregation at prayer. OIC SOURCING GAP — the feed carries this event only through NDTV (India); no Dawn, Geo or Express Tribune copy of the bombing appears, which is flagged for feed-side audit.

stories.label: LHC extends suspension of PMDC directive for Afghan medical students' return
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court has again suspended a Pakistan Medical and Dental Council directive ordering Afghan medical students to return to Afghanistan — the students stay enrolled only because a court keeps pausing a regulator. Lead with what the directive would actually do: send women studying medicine back to a country where the Taliban has banned women from medical education entirely, which means the order is not a visa formality but a termination of their training. Teach the mechanism: the PMDC regulates registration, not immigration, so a council directive is being used to achieve a removal that the interior ministry would have to justify differently — report which statute PMDC invoked, how many students are affected, what their legal status in Pakistan is, and what the universities say. Then the structural why: Pakistan's post-2023 repatriation drive has treated long-settled Afghans as reversible guests, and the education of a generation of Afghan doctors is one of the few things that survived the last four years of that policy. Report the next hearing date, what PMDC's counsel has yet to file, and what the students themselves say. Who holds power: a regulator, a court and a ministry, none of whom has to answer to the people affected. Regional sourcing satisfied: Dawn (PK).

stories.label: Why One Saudi Pipeline Is Crucial to the Global Oil Market
stories.summary: With Hormuz still contested, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was the one relief valve moving crude across the peninsula to the Red Sea — and it has now shut down. Lead with the geography, because it is the whole argument: the line runs about 1,200km from Abqaiq to Yanbu, and its capacity — roughly 5 million barrels a day, which Aramco says improvements had raised toward 7 — is the only way Saudi barrels reach a customer without passing a strait someone can close. Teach what a relief valve is worth: without it, Riyadh's export options are Hormuz, which is the problem, or north to Suez and the Mediterranean, which is the wrong direction for Asian buyers who take most of the oil. Report why the line is down, who says so, when Aramco expects it back, and what actually happened at the Red Sea end, attributing carefully — reports of a strike on the line are circulating and must be sourced, not assumed. Then the consequence for our reader: Brent above $100 is not a sentiment story, it is a routing story, and the countries that pay first are oil-importing developing economies buying dollars-denominated crude with weakening currencies. Continues our Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint coverage — this is the third chokepoint in the same system, and it is a pipe, not a strait. OIC SOURCING GAP: no Arab News, Al Jazeera or Gulf outlet carries this in today's feed.

stories.label: Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
stories.summary: Buffett, 96, becomes chairman emeritus and his son Howard takes the chair — while Greg Abel runs the company as chief executive. Lead with that split, because it is the mechanism and it is unusual: Berkshire has deliberately separated the guardian of the culture from the operator of the business, giving a non-executive family chairman the power to remove a CEO who changes what the company is. Teach why that structure exists at all — Berkshire's defence against the thing that destroys conglomerates, which is a successor who starts trading the balance sheet — and report the dual-class share arithmetic, because Buffett's remaining A shares and their voting weight decide whether the chairmanship is real authority or ceremony. Report what the letter to shareholders actually said, Howard Buffett's board tenure since 1993 and what he does outside Berkshire, and how the shares moved. Then the part worth our reader's attention rather than the obituary framing: Berkshire holds one of the largest cash positions in corporate history, so the succession question is really who decides where several hundred billion dollars goes in a market with Brent above $100 and yields rising. Avoid hagiography — report the structure, the numbers and the unresolved question of what the cash is for.

stories.label: Noel Tata vs N Chandrasekaran? Inside their tense Tata Group ties
stories.summary: Chandrasekaran has been reappointed chairman of Tata Sons for five more years, a month after saying he would step down — and the reappointment has split the board from Tata Trusts, which owns the majority of the company. Lead with the ownership fact, because it is the mechanism almost no coverage explains: India's largest conglomerate is controlled not by shareholders or a family but by philanthropic trusts holding roughly 66% of the holding company, so the people who appoint the chairman answer to a charitable purpose rather than to investors. Teach what that means in practice — trustees nominate directors, the trusts hold an effective veto, and the same structure produced the Mistry removal in 2016 and the litigation that followed to the Supreme Court. Report who voted which way, what Noel Tata's position as trusts chairman gives him, whether a nominee-director convention was honoured, and what both sides have said on the record. Then the stake for our reader: this group runs steel, vehicles, airlines, salt and a semiconductor fab, employs hundreds of thousands, and a governance fight over who names its chairman is a fight over where India's largest private capital allocation goes. Report whether Tata Sons' delayed listing is part of the dispute — it is the financial pressure underneath the personalities.

stories.label: Indonesian Parliamentary Committee Debates Changes to Fiscal Deficit Limit
stories.summary: Indonesian lawmakers are debating whether to let the government spend past the statutory 3% deficit ceiling to fund its expansive agenda. Lead with what the 3% rule actually is and where it came from, because that is the story: the cap was written into law after the 1997-98 Asian financial crisis, when Indonesia's debt-to-GDP ratio exploded and the IMF programme that followed cost the government its economic sovereignty — the limit is a promise made to the country's own future, not a technocratic preference. Teach the mechanism: a statutory cap binds differently from a policy target, because breaching it requires parliament to amend the law in public, which is precisely the friction it was designed to create. Report which committee, what change is proposed, the current deficit and debt ratios, what the free-meals and other flagship programmes cost, and what the finance ministry, Bank Indonesia and the rating agencies have said. Then the consequence for our reader: Indonesia is the largest Muslim-majority economy and a bellwether for emerging-market borrowing costs at a moment when the Bank of Japan has just ended free yen and global yields are rising — a country that loosens its own fiscal anchor into that is paying for it in the bond market, so report what the rupiah and the 10-year have done. Who is affected: Indonesians, through whichever side of the trade-off — programmes or borrowing costs — gives way. OIC SOURCING GAP: no Jakarta Post or Indonesian outlet covers this in today's feed. Fills the audit's flagged Southeast Asia gap.

stories.label: UK's Ayan Capital raises $100 million ahead of banking licence application
stories.summary: A UK Islamic fintech has raised $100 million specifically to clear the capital threshold for a banking licence application. Lead with why the raise had to come first: the Prudential Regulation Authority requires a mobilisation-stage bank to hold real capital before it can take a single deposit, so for a Sharia-compliant institution the licence is bought with equity rather than earned with a deposit base — which is why Britain has only a handful of fully licensed Islamic banks despite the largest Muslim population in western Europe. Teach the structural constraint our reader will actually want: an Islamic bank cannot use the interest-bearing instruments that let a conventional bank manage liquidity, and the Bank of England's Alternative Liquidity Facility exists precisely because of that gap — report whether Ayan intends to use it. Report who led the round, what the capital target for authorisation is, where Ayan sits in the process, and what products it plans. Then the consequence: British Muslims have been served mainly by home-purchase plans priced above conventional mortgages, so the test of this licence is whether scale narrows that spread or reproduces it. Who holds power: a regulator whose rulebook was written for a different balance sheet. Report the company's own numbers with attribution — this is a single-source announcement and should read as one.

stories.label: First for RNA therapy: man with rare motor-neuron disease improves after treatment
stories.summary: A physician with an uncommon motor neuron disease is still working a year after becoming the first person given a drug designed against his own specific mutation — and he improved, which almost never happens in this class of disease. Lead with the improvement, because motor neuron disease is defined by one-way decline and a reversal is the finding. Teach the mechanism precisely: an antisense oligonucleotide is a short synthetic strand of nucleic acid that binds the messenger RNA carrying a faulty instruction and marks it for destruction before a protein is ever made — it does not edit the genome, it silences one transcript, which is why it must be dosed repeatedly and why it can be designed against a mutation found in a single patient. Report the mutation, the journal, the authors' own caution about an n of one, and what the follow-up plan is. Then the part that matters beyond this man: the bottleneck on bespoke ASOs is no longer chemistry but regulation and cost — a drug made for one person has no market, so report what it cost, who paid, and what regulatory pathway was used, because that is what decides whether this reaches anyone in a country without a rare-disease programme. Who holds power: regulators and the handful of labs that can synthesise and test these at clinical grade. Do not write this as a cure.

stories.label: Canadian courts take police misconduct seriously, but researchers say sentencing alone can't fix a broken system
stories.summary: The first large-scale empirical study of how Canadian courts sentence police officers convicted of breaching public trust finds the courts do treat it as an aggravating factor — and that this changes very little. Lead with the number the researchers actually produced: how many convictions they found across the period studied, which is almost certainly small relative to the complaints filed, because the finding hiding inside a sentencing study is how few cases ever reach a judge. Teach the mechanism our reader can carry to any country: sentencing is the last and narrowest filter in a chain — complaint, investigation, charge, conviction, sentence — and each earlier stage is controlled by bodies with institutional reasons to stop the case, so a court that sentences firmly is disciplining the handful of officers the system already decided to surrender. Report the authors, the journal (Police Quarterly), the method, the sample, and what they say the alternative to sentencing reform is. Then why it belongs here rather than in a Canadian paper: this is the empirical shape of the accountability gap we describe every time security forces kill someone — the NSCDC custody deaths in Nigeria, the stray-bullet killings during military operations — and a rigorous measurement of that gap in a country with functioning courts is the strongest available evidence about what courts alone can and cannot do. Attribute the researchers' conclusions as theirs.

stories.label: SARD: A Large-Scale Synthetic Arabic OCR Dataset for Book-Style Text Recognition
stories.summary: A new open dataset puts 2,621,075 synthetic Arabic document images and 794.6 million words, rendered in six fonts, into the public domain for training OCR. Lead with the scale and then with why it had to be synthetic, because that is the mechanism: Arabic OCR has lagged Latin-script OCR by years not for lack of interest but for lack of labelled data, and labelled data is expensive precisely where the languages are poorest in research funding — so generating pages with known ground truth is how you escape a bottleneck you cannot buy your way out of. Teach what makes Arabic hard for a recogniser: it is cursive and connected, letters change shape by position in the word, diacritics sit above and below the line, and book typography stacks ligatures — a segmentation model built for spaced Latin glyphs simply does not apply. Report the fonts used, the licence, the baseline results the authors report, and their own statement of the limitation, which is that synthetic pages do not have the stains, skew and bleed-through of a real scanned book. Then the stake for our reader: the Arabic manuscript and print heritage sitting undigitised in libraries from Cairo to Istanbul to Timbuktu is inaccessible to search for exactly this reason, and a free dataset is the input that lets a researcher anywhere build the recogniser rather than wait for a vendor to. Who holds power: whoever owns the archives, once the text becomes searchable.

stories.label: US and China Vie for AI Lead Before Trump-Xi Summit
stories.summary: Both governments are positioning their AI industries ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting, and the thing being negotiated is not models but silicon. Lead with the concrete lever rather than the summit theatre: US export controls set a compute threshold above which Nvidia cannot sell into China, so Washington's bargaining chip is a performance number in a regulation, and Beijing's counter is domestic accelerators plus control of the rare-earth and packaging inputs the US supply chain still needs. Teach the mechanism our technically literate reader will want — a controlled-part rule bites at the interconnect and memory bandwidth as much as at raw FLOPS, which is why cut-down export parts keep getting re-cut, and why smuggling and offshore cloud access are the loopholes that make the control leakier than it reads. Report what each side has actually announced this week, which companies are named, what the summit's stated agenda is, and what the export-control agency has said, attributing each. Then the part that concerns everyone who is neither American nor Chinese: countries buying AI capacity — the Gulf states building data centres, Indonesia, Malaysia, India — are being asked to choose a stack, and a compute licence regime run from Washington means a third country's AI capability is subject to a licence it does not hold. Report what conditions have been attached to Gulf and Southeast Asian chip deals, because that is where this lands for our reader.

stories.label: USMC Used Its Expeditionary Operations Playbook In Combat For First Time During Epic Fury
stories.summary: The US Marine Corps has used its expeditionary advanced base doctrine in combat for the first time during the Iran campaign — remote forward refuelling and rearming points for F-35Bs, plus dispersed sensing sites. Lead with what the doctrine is for, because it explains a decade of procurement: the Corps rebuilt itself around the assumption that large fixed airbases are now targetable by precision missiles, so it disperses into many small temporary sites that can be occupied for hours and abandoned. Teach the mechanics our reader will find genuinely new — a FARP is fuel bladders, ordnance and a few Marines, so the limiting factor is not aircraft but the logistics aircraft that seed the site, and the whole scheme trades sortie rate for survivability. Report what TWZ documents actually happened: which sites, which aircraft, what the Corps says, and what it does not say. Then the part that belongs in our pages rather than a defence trade's: these sites sit on someone's territory. A dispersed basing doctrine converts Gulf and Red Sea littoral states into temporary launch geography, and the consent question — which government agreed to what, and whether any parliament was told — is the accountability story underneath the engineering. Report who hosted, if it is reported, and say plainly where it is not. Who is affected: people under the flight paths those sites shorten.
